From: Amanda Albright <amandaalbright@bedrocktx.com>
Sent: Friday, October 16, 2026 3:18 AM
To: President HOA <president@canyongateatcincoranch.com>
Cc: Treasurer HOA <treasurer@canyongateatcincoranch.com>; Vice President HOA <vicepresident@canyongateatcincoranch.com>; Director HOA <director@canyongateatcincoranch.com>; Secretary HOA <secretary@canyongateatcincoranch.com>; Ed Gojara <egojara@bedrocktx.com>
Subject: RE: Camera Proposals


Good morning Hugh and Board,
I completed my review of the security camera proposals against the direction you provided: Canyon Gate wants to purchase and own the equipment, have it professionally installed, maintain reliable access to live and recorded video, and avoid paying for active monitoring that the Association does not want.
Based on that review, I recommend moving forward with iTech’s updated 2026 proposal as the preferred solution, subject to several final scope and contract confirmations before the Association signs or releases funds.
I do not recommend beginning another full bidding cycle at this point. With multiple cameras already down, continuing concerns about camera angles, the recent gate incident, and installation availability already extending into December, there is a cost and risk associated with delay as well.
WHY I RECOMMEND ITECH
---------------------
The current iTech proposal is $44,619.75 plus tax, with 50% due upon acceptance and 50% upon completion.
Its approach is practical. Rather than replacing the entire existing system, iTech proposes to reuse 10 clubhouse cameras and 3 guard-house cameras that remain usable, replace deficient cameras, add new coverage, replace the recording infrastructure with two 12TB Digital Watchdog servers, and add the necessary switches, backup power and network connectivity.
It also addresses some of the Board’s current concerns by adjusting existing camera views and adding or replacing coverage at the clubhouse, guard house, basketball pavilion and rear entrance.
That is much closer to the system the Board has described wanting than the Envera alternative.
WHY I AM NOT RECOMMENDING ENVERA AS CURRENTLY PROPOSED
------------------------------------------------------
Envera’s proposal is $60,087.53 upfront plus $2,453.54 per month and requires a minimum 60-month service commitment.
That equates to approximately $207,300 before tax over five years.
The package also includes recurring camera, licensing, maintenance and active-monitoring services. That may be appropriate for a community looking for a fully managed monitoring service, but it does not align well with the Board’s stated objective of purchasing the system without active monitoring.
The Envera quote also expired on August 31, 2026, so it would need to be refreshed before it could be accepted.
If the Board wants Envera maintained as a fallback, we can obtain revised pricing for a purchase/access-only configuration, but I would not delay the iTech diligence waiting on that unless the Board specifically wants Envera reconsidered.
OTHER PROPOSALS
---------------
I am treating the earlier $38,211.02 iTech proposal as historical reference rather than a third current alternative.
The updated 2026 proposal is more detailed and reflects a revised scope, so the difference between the two prices should not be viewed simply as the same system becoming approximately $6,400 more expensive.
The Netwatch materials are also useful because they provide another view of the physical coverage requirements and specifically contemplate 30 days of video retention.
However, the Netwatch design includes monitored cameras and after-hours monitoring, which does not match the Board’s current direction. The materials I reviewed also do not contain a complete priced proposal that can be compared directly with iTech and Envera.
I would use Netwatch as useful design and coverage information, but I would not delay the project treating it as a third executable bid.
IMPORTANT RISKS AND OPEN ITEMS WITH ITECH
-----------------------------------------
Although iTech is my preferred vendor, I would not recommend signing the proposal exactly as presented today.
1. PRICE / CHANGE-ORDER EXPOSURE
The proposal is described as a budgetary bid. iTech also intends to conduct a pre-installation site survey and acknowledges existing faults in the current system that may require troubleshooting and potentially result in change orders.
For a project of this size, I do not want Canyon Gate exposed to an open-ended cost.
I recommend requiring written Association approval before any additional work or change order is performed, and preferably obtaining either a final confirmed price following the survey or an agreed not-to-exceed amount.
2. CLOUD ACCESS VS. CLOUD STORAGE
The proposal provides two 12TB local recording servers. iTech’s optional $440 per month maintenance and system-health plan includes video sharing and secure web/cloud access.
What is not clear is:
- Whether remote access is available without the $440 plan
- Whether recorded video is actually stored in the cloud or the cloud simply provides remote access to locally stored footage
- Whether cloud storage/access can be purchased without monitoring
- What recurring cost, if any, applies to the configuration Canyon Gate actually wants
Cloud access and cloud storage are not the same thing, and I want that distinction resolved before the Board commits.
3. RECORDING RETENTION
The proposal does not clearly state how many days of recorded footage the proposed system will retain.
The Board should know whether the expected retention is 15 days, 30 days, 60 days, or another period under normal recording settings.
I recommend requiring a minimum expected retention period in writing.
4. WARRANTY COVERAGE
The optional maintenance plan discusses replacement and loaner equipment for warranty issues, but I want the underlying equipment and workmanship warranties documented separately.
The Board should know exactly what protection exists if Canyon Gate does not purchase the $440 monthly plan.
5. EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE
The proposal assumes adequate electrical power is available and that existing surveillance wiring can be used as anticipated.
If those assumptions prove incorrect, additional work and cost may be necessary.
Those potential issues should be identified during the site survey rather than after the project is underway.
6. OPTIONAL MAINTENANCE / MONITORING PLAN
iTech offers an optional $440 per month maintenance and system-health plan.
Based on the Board’s direction, I am not recommending that Canyon Gate add this service unless iTech confirms that some portion of it is necessary to obtain the remote access or cloud functionality the Board wants.
The first question I would resolve with iTech is whether Canyon Gate can purchase the equipment and installation, retain remote access to live and recorded video, and obtain the desired storage/retention without enrolling in an ongoing monitoring program.
If those functions can be provided separately, I would recommend excluding the $440 monthly plan.
CONTRACT AND LIABILITY ITEMS TO RESOLVE
---------------------------------------
Before execution, I recommend obtaining or confirming the following:
- Final scope and camera-location plan following the site survey
- Final equipment list and model numbers
- Written confirmation that the configuration contains no active monitoring unless separately approved by the Board
- Remote-access and cloud-storage terms and pricing
- Expected video-retention period
- Equipment and workmanship warranties
- Current installation schedule and confirmation of the December availability
- Written change-order approval procedures
- Responsibility for unexpected wiring, electrical or network deficiencies
- Certificate of insurance and vendor compliance documentation
- Ownership of the equipment, recordings, credentials and system configuration
- Canyon Gate’s right to access and export its recordings if the vendor relationship ends
- Data-security and privacy obligations
- Indemnification and limitation-of-liability provisions
- Acceptance and system testing before final payment
- Any termination, renewal or cancellation provisions applicable to recurring services
I do not view these as reasons to stop the project. I view them as normal protections that should be addressed before Canyon Gate signs a material technology and security contract.
FINANCIAL CONSIDERATIONS
------------------------
I am also mindful that this decision does not occur in isolation.
The Association has recently approved an assessment increase, and the Board is balancing a number of community needs and capital priorities.
We need to address legitimate security and infrastructure needs while also being fiscally responsible and demonstrating to homeowners that Association funds are being spent carefully.
That is another reason I favor the iTech direction.
The current iTech equipment and installation proposal is $44,619.75 plus tax.
By comparison, Envera’s current proposal is approximately $207,300 before tax over its required five-year term.
Because the Board has specifically stated that it does not want monitoring, I am not including iTech’s optional $440 monthly monitoring/maintenance plan as part of my recommended configuration unless iTech establishes that some portion of that service is required for the remote access or cloud functionality the Board wants.
My objective would be to preserve the functionality Canyon Gate actually needs while avoiding recurring costs for services the Board has said it does not want.
TrustEd’s current accounting information is still being reconciled as part of our transition, so I am treating current cash and reserve figures as provisional rather than representing a particular balance as definitively available for this project.
The final funding source should be verified before the contract is executed.
MY RECOMMENDATION
-----------------
Preferred vendor: iTech
Project recommendation: Proceed
Additional full bidding round: Not recommended at this time
Contract readiness: Conditional, not yet ready to sign
Urgency: High
I recommend that we move forward with iTech now as the preferred vendor, resolve the remaining items promptly, and then bring the Board the final contract and approval package.
If the Board is comfortable with this direction, I can communicate directly with iTech to resolve the remaining scope, cloud-access, storage, warranty, change-order, insurance and contract questions.
I would limit that communication to non-binding diligence and clarification only. I would not accept the proposal, authorize work, approve a change order, or otherwise commit the Association without the appropriate Board approval.
Once those items are resolved, I can update the analysis and bring the Board back a final recommendation and approval package.
Assuming iTech confirms that Canyon Gate can obtain the requested equipment, installation, remote access and appropriate video retention without an unwanted monitoring commitment, confirms the installation schedule, and addresses the remaining contract protections without materially changing the economics, I would recommend final approval rather than delaying the project for another bidding cycle.
That gives us a path to address the security problem quickly while still protecting the Association financially and contractually.
Amanda Albright
Senior Community Manager
Bedrock Association Management — Canyon Gate at Cinco Ranch
amanda@bedrocktx.com · (832) 588-2485
